issues.title: Internal class missing sealed keyword
issues.description: Internal implementation classes that are not designed for inheritance must be marked with the 'sealed' keyword. The WebSocketWrapper class is an internal implementation class that should be sealed to prevent unintended subclassing.
issues.rule_name: Sealed Keyword Required for Internal Implementation Classes

issues.title: Incorrect boolean operator in regex validation
issues.description: The test assertion uses AND (&&) operator instead of OR (||) when checking if the log message matches either the old or new CSP error pattern. This causes the test to fail because a log message cannot simultaneously match both regex patterns - they represent different browser error message formats. The original intent was to accept either format, but the AND operator requires both patterns to match at the same time, which is impossible. This will cause the test to fail even when receiving a valid CSP error message in either format.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
Assert.True(
    ParseErrorMessageRegexOld.IsMatch(logs[0].Message) &&
    ParseErrorMessageRegexNew.IsMatch(logs[0].Message),
    $"Expected log message to match one of the CSP error patterns: {ParseErrorMessageRegexOld} or {ParseErrorMessageRegexNew}. Actual: {logs[0].Message}");

issues.title: Disposal order causing potential race condition
issues.description: The connection disposal order is reversed - disposing secondConnection before the connection that is still being used. In the test, 'connection' performs an InvokeAsync call and its TaskCompletionSource (tcs) is awaited immediately before disposal. However, disposing secondConnection first may cause premature cleanup of shared resources or message handlers since both connections share the same user ('*'). This can lead to flaky test behavior where the connection's pending operations are interrupted by the disposal of secondConnection, especially in distributed scenarios where both connections interact with the same Redis backplane.

issues.title: Race condition from premature TaskCompletionSource recreation
issues.description: The _receiveTcs TaskCompletionSource is recreated before checking if the buffer is zero-sized, creating a race condition in the WebSocketWrapper's ReceiveAsync implementation. When a zero-byte read occurs (buffer.Count == 0), the method returns early with the result but the TCS has already been reset. This means if another thread or the background task tries to set a result on the now-recreated TCS while this zero-byte read is in progress, it will affect the next receive operation rather than completing the current one. This breaks the synchronization contract and can cause message loss or out-of-order receives in the stateful reconnection test scenarios where WebSocket message sequencing is critical.

issues.title: Test method missing Arrange/Act/Assert comments
issues.description: The modified test method does not contain explicit '// Arrange', '// Act', and '// Assert' (or '// Act & Assert') comments to delineate phases, violating the required AAA comment pattern.
issues.rule_name: Test Methods Must Use Arrange-Act-Assert Pattern with Comments

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64685 - [release/9.0] Update dependencies from dotnet/arcade
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR bumps the dotnet/arcade dependency set from 9.0.0-beta.25562.4 to 9.0.0-beta.25626.6 (SHA 6e2d8e20 to ab5773ac). The version pins are consistent across eng/Version.Details.xml, eng/Versions.props and global.json. It also syncs eng/common scripts: source-build now targets 1es-azurelinux-3 and ci.dot.net/internal, the PowerShell scripts use -UseBasicParsing, LocateVisualStudio is null-safe when global.json lacks tools.vs, and the source-index stage1 job defaults to running only on main.

Mixed into the bump are test-only changes that have nothing to do with dependencies: new QuarantinedTest attributes on two RedisEndToEnd tests, a reordered DisposeAsync, a modified WebSocketWrapper.ReceiveAsync, and a rewritten CSP assertion in WebSocketCompressionTests. The CSP assertion is broken: it uses && where the message says "one of", so it can never pass. The WebSocketWrapper edit also changes zero-byte read semantics and can drop a buffered message. Both need fixing before merge.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The dependency bump itself is clean and internally consistent. The blocking problem is the CSP assertion in WebSocketCompressionTests.cs, which requires both browser message formats to match a single log line, so the test will always fail. The WebSocketWrapper reordering is a silent behaviour change in test infrastructure that is unrelated to the bump and should be reverted or justified. The remaining items are low-risk hygiene.

architecture.overview:
The Arcade SDK is pinned in three places that must agree: eng/Version.Details.xml (the Maestro-managed source of truth), eng/Versions.props (MSBuild properties consumed by the product projects and the source-build intermediate), and global.json msbuild-sdks (which resolves Microsoft.DotNet.Arcade.Sdk and Microsoft.DotNet.Helix.Sdk at evaluation time). This PR moves all three to 9.0.0-beta.25626.6 with the same commit SHA, so the pins stay aligned.

The eng/common/ tree is a vendored copy of Arcade's engineering scripts and pipeline templates. This PR refreshes it. The source-build job now uses the 1es-azurelinux-3 image and the ci.dot.net/internal runtime feed, which matches the feed the rest of the repo already uses. The PowerShell helpers gain -UseBasicParsing and a null-safe Visual Studio lookup. Separately, two SignalR Redis end-to-end tests and one Components E2E assertion are edited directly. Those edits are not dependency-driven.
steps: Entry point: global.json msbuild-sdks resolves the Arcade and Helix SDKs, and eng/Version.Details.xml is the Maestro-managed record. Both now point at 9.0.0-beta.25626.6.
eng/Versions.props exposes the same version as MSBuild properties (MicrosoftDotNetBuildTasksInstallersVersion, MicrosoftSourceBuildIntermediatearcadeVersion and similar) for the product projects.
eng/common/core-templates/steps/source-build.yml and job/source-build.yml pick up the new feed host and the azurelinux image for internal source-build pools.
eng/common/tools.ps1 gets -UseBasicParsing on every Invoke-WebRequest and a guarded LocateVisualStudio that no longer dereferences a missing global.json tools.vs.
Test-only edits: WebSocketCompressionTests.cs replaces a single CSP regex with two, RedisEndToEnd.cs adds QuarantinedTest attributes and changes the WebSocketWrapper receive path.

findings.title: CSP assertion uses AND, so the test can never pass
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/test/E2ETest/ServerExecutionTests/WebSocketCompressionTests.cs`, the assertion at lines 107-110 in `EmbeddingServerAppInsideIframe_WithCompressionEnabled_Fails` combines `ParseErrorMessageRegexOld.IsMatch(...)` and `ParseErrorMessageRegexNew.IsMatch(...)` with `&&`. Those patterns match mutually exclusive browser wordings, so the assertion can never succeed. Change the operator to `||` so the test passes when either the old or the new CSP violation message is logged. Keep the existing failure message, which already says "one of". Do not change the regex definitions.

findings.title: WebSocketWrapper reset moved ahead of zero-byte check drops buffered messages
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/SignalR/server/StackExchangeRedis/test/RedisEndToEnd.cs`, `WebSocketWrapper.ReceiveAsync` (lines ~406-417) now resets `_receiveTcs` before the zero-byte early return. A zero-byte read therefore consumes the buffered message and drops its payload, and the next real read waits forever for a new frame. Move the `_receiveTcs = new(...)` assignment back below the `if (buffer.Count == 0) return` block, so it runs only after the payload is copied. Keep the existing "Handle zero-byte reads" comment. Confirm the stateful reconnect test in the same file still passes. If the reorder was intentional, document the reason in a comment.

findings.title: Unrelated test-policy changes ride along with the dependency bump
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/SignalR/server/StackExchangeRedis/test/RedisEndToEnd.cs`, the `[QuarantinedTest(...)]` attributes at lines 92 and 188 and the DisposeAsync reordering at lines ~213-214 are test-policy and test-logic changes that are not part of the Arcade dependency bump. Remove them from this PR, or, if they are required for the release branch, add a PR description section that explains each one and links the referenced issues (59991, 63582). Keep the dependency bump diff limited to the eng/ and global.json changes.

findings.title: WebSocketWrapper visibility loosened from sealed without a reason
findings.body:
`WebSocketWrapper` changes from `internal sealed class` to `internal class`. Nothing in the diff subclasses it, and removing `sealed` opens the type to inheritance without any stated need. Unless a subclass is planned, restore `sealed`.

::diff{file="src/SignalR/server/StackExchangeRedis/test/RedisEndToEnd.cs" lines="362-362"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/SignalR/server/StackExchangeRedis/test/RedisEndToEnd.cs` line 362, `WebSocketWrapper` was changed from `internal sealed class` to `internal class` with no subclass in the codebase. Restore `sealed` to match the original declaration, unless a subclass is needed and the reason is documented.

findings.title: Redundant else branch in LocateVisualStudio
findings.body:
Inside `if (!$vsRequirements) { ... }`, the `else { $vsRequirements = $null }` branch does nothing, because `$vsRequirements` is already falsy there. The guard can be a single `if`. The later `-and` checks already handle the null case.

::diff{file="eng/common/tools.ps1" lines="550-556"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `eng/common/tools.ps1` in `LocateVisualStudio` (lines 550-556), simplify the block to: if `$vsRequirements` is falsy and `$GlobalJson.tools` has a `vs` member, assign `$vsRequirements = $GlobalJson.tools.vs`. Drop the redundant `else { $vsRequirements = $null }`. The existing `-and` guards on the later `version` and `components` checks already handle a null value.

findings.title: Internal source-build image switched to an unverified pool image
findings.fixPrompt: In `eng/common/core-templates/job/source-build.yml` at line 68, the internal source-build pool image was changed to `1es-azurelinux-3`. Before merging, confirm with the DNCEng pool owners that `NetCore1ESPool-Internal` and `NetCore1ESPool-Svc-Internal` offer that image. Also confirm that the release/9.0 internal source-build job still runs. If the image is unavailable, keep the upstream value or coordinate a pool update. Do not edit the template locally, because eng/common is vendored from Arcade.

findings.title: Arcade pins are internally consistent
findings.body:
`eng/Version.Details.xml`, `eng/Versions.props` and `global.json` all move to `9.0.0-beta.25626.6` and SHA `ab5773ac30dce73227fa1dff6bf1a21eea67cbd0`. The Arcade.Sdk, Helix.Sdk, Build.Tasks.Installers, Build.Tasks.Templating, RemoteExecutor and SourceBuild.Intermediate.arcade entries match each other. The version properties used by the projects match the Version.Details entries, so Maestro and the MSBuild props stay in sync.

::diff{file="eng/Versions.props" lines="169-172"}

findings.title: Source-build feed host now matches the rest of the repo
findings.body:
The source-build step moves from `dotnetbuilds.blob.core.windows.net/internal` to `ci.dot.net/internal`. That makes it consistent with `.azure/pipelines/ci.yml`, `eng/helix/helix.proj`, `Product.targets` and `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.csproj`, which already use `ci.dot.net/internal`. Before this change the source-build path was the one outlier.

::diff{file="eng/common/core-templates/steps/source-build.yml" lines="43-44"}

findings.title: Source-index stage1 default gated to main, a no-op for this repo
findings.body:
The `condition` default in `job/source-index-stage1.yml` changes from `''` to `eq(variables['Build.SourceBranch'], 'refs/heads/main')`. In this repo `.azure/pipelines/ci.yml` already sets `enableSourceIndex` only on main, so the behaviour is unchanged here. Other Arcade consumers that rely on running source index from release branches will see a difference, so the change is worth knowing about.

::diff{file="eng/common/core-templates/job/source-index-stage1.yml" lines="9-9"}

findings.title: Visual Studio lookup no longer crashes when global.json lacks tools.vs
findings.body:
The guarded `Get-Member` checks mean `LocateVisualStudio` no longer dereferences a missing `tools.vs` and no longer calls `Get-Member` on a null `$vsRequirements`. The `version` and `components` checks are guarded by a null test first. This is a real robustness fix for repos whose global.json omits the `vs` block.

::diff{file="eng/common/tools.ps1" lines="543-576"}

findings.title: -UseBasicParsing added to Invoke-WebRequest calls
findings.body:
Each `Invoke-WebRequest` call in `tools.ps1`, `internal-feed-operations.ps1` and `nuget-verification.ps1` now passes `-UseBasicParsing`. On Windows PowerShell 5.1 this avoids a dependency on the IE DOM engine, which fails on machines without it, and it is a harmless no-op on PowerShell 7+. Good hygiene for CI agents.

::diff{file="eng/common/tools.ps1" lines="269-269"}
